newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean students battle riot police in Kwangju.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean students battle riot police in Kwangju.

text.p: Student violence erupted in the South Korean city of Kwangju on Friday as residents prepared to mourn victims of a 1980 army massacre in the first officially-sponsored anniversary ceremonies.
More than 300 students wielding iron bars and hurling molotov cocktails fought pitched battles with riot police around Chosun University, witnesses said.
They were among a crowd of 3,000 students who had massed inside the campus for funeral rites to honour a student who died of a heart attack during anti-government protests in March.
Funeral ceremonies were timed to coincide with Sunday's anniversary of the massacre of pro-democracy students, a tragedy that has left deep scars on South Korea.
Riot police fired volleys of tear gas to prevent the students marching into the streets, witnesses said. Students had prepared an arsenal of thousands of firebombs.
The coffin of the student was draped with the South Korean national flag and placed on the back of a truck on the campus.

This year's anniversary of the Kwangju massacre has added significance since the main perpetrators of the killings, former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, are now behind bars along with a handful of former generals.
The two were jailed at the end of 1995 on charges of mutiny, treason and corruption. Chun was sentenced to life in prison and Roh to 17 years, and final appeals were dismissed in April.

Some 200 people were killed by official count when paratroopers stormed the city in 1980 to put down a revolt against martial law declared by then general Chun. Some residents put the death toll as high as 2,000.

Remains of those killed have been moved to a newly-built cemetery in Kwangju, where they will be honoured as heroes on Sunday in a nationally-televised ceremony presided over by Prime Minister Koh Kun.
